events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands or falls on NS-1: the driver must have tapped "I'm Here" while inside the pickup radius, then waited continuously more than 3 minutes inside that radius before cancelling. events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the driver, so the fee's validity runs through NS-0 to NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. Both sides now converge on the arithmetic: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 while 41 m from the pickup, satisfying NS-1 (i) and (ii), but the wait after that tap ran only to the 14:15:50 cancellation [F6][F4][NS-1]. That is 1 min 40 s inside the radius; even measured from the platform-recorded arrival at 14:13:25 it is 2 min 25 s, and the stationary window was only 2 min 0 s [F5][F2][F3][NS-1]. NS-1 (iii) requires more than 3 minutes continuously at the pickup after the arrival confirmation, so the requirement fails on every reading of the record.

Because NS-1 (i)(ii) are met but (iii) is not, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full [F7][NS-2]. The amount is fixed by the fare fact: cancellation fee charged $6.61, surge 1.0× so no other charge is in play [F7][F8][NS-2]. The driver's chat "3 min up, cancelling the trip" and his post-trip statement that he waited and cancelled as a no-show are statements, and they yield to the system timeline [F10][F12][F6][F4]; they do not create the missing waiting time.

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled and the $6.61 cancellation fee stands or falls on NS-1: the driver must have tapped "I'm Here" while inside the pickup radius, then waited continuously more than 3 minutes inside that radius before cancelling. The system records show he tapped at 14:14:10 and cancelled at 14:15:50, i.e. only 1 min 40 s later (F6).

Even measured from the platform-recorded arrival rather than the tap, the driver spent only 2 min 25 s within 200 m of the pickup before cancelling (first within 200 m at 14:13:25, cancellation at 14:15:50), which is below the > 3 minutes required; total time inside the radius before cancellation was 2 min 25 s (F5, F2).

The driver's own chat message at 14:15 admits the wait fell short: he wrote "3 min up, cancelling the trip" only about one minute after his 14:14 "I'm here" message (F10, F9), so nothing in the record supports a continuous wait exceeding three minutes inside the pickup zone.

Because NS-1's timing condition is not met, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full; the fee on record is $6.61 with no surge (F4, F7, F8), so the refund amount is exactly $6.61 computed from the cancellation-fee fact F7.

No justification supplied by the driver displaces this: there were no traffic speed-band records and no incidents near the route during the trip window, and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F13, F14, F15), so the cancellation was not forced by any recorded condition.

The rider's own record supports her: 1189-day account, 4.7 rating and no no-show disputes upheld against her in 90 days (F16), while the driver already has one no-show dispute upheld in the last 90 days alongside 2 disputes and 815 trips (F17). I ask the judge to add flag_account for review of the driver's use of the arrival/cancellation button (Ryde treats abuse of that button as fraudulent conduct); the profile fact is offered only as the basis for that additional action, not as the finding on the fee.

weaknesses: The driver did genuinely approach and wait: closest approach 38 m at 14:15:35 and stationary 2 min 0 s at 41 m from the pickup (F1, F3). The other side will argue he substantially performed the wait and that the 1 min 40 s shortfall is technical.
He did tap "I'm Here" at 41 m, within the 200 m radius (F6), so NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied; the rider's case rests entirely on the 3-minute duration element (iii).

His chat message says the trip was cancelled as a no-show and his written statement repeats that version (F10, F12); although statements lose to the system records (F2, F5, F6), the judge may still read his conduct as a good-faith no-show rather than button abuse.
The rider has 1 dispute in the last 90 days (F16), which the driver could use to suggest a pattern of fee complaints even though none was upheld.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here": the timeline records a driver tap at 14:14:10 (not a platform auto-arrival, which is separately recorded at 14:13:25), and the driver announced it in chat at 14:14 ("I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel").
At the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the driver was 41 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 (ii) is satisfied.

The rider complains the driver "cancelled after barely two minutes", but the record contradicts her: the platform logged arrival at 14:13:25 and cancellation at 14:15:50 — 2 min 25 s of cumulative waiting inside 200 m, and the 2-minute period she may be counting is only the stationary window 14:13:50–14:15:50, which starts after, not at, arrival.

Even without the platform's auto-arrival time, time run from the driver's own "I'm Here" tap at 14:14:10 to cancellation at 14:15:50 is 1 min 40 s, which is short of the default 3 minutes — the honest driver-side weakness in this case.

The driver's contemporaneous messages are consistent and uncoached: a single arrival notice at 14:14 and a single cancellation notice at 14:15, with the complete chat record (2 messages, all timestamped) containing no demand for a fee, no abuse and no pressure on the rider — nothing in the file reads as a threat, intimidation or dangerous-driving allegation, so the case does not need to be routed to a person under SAFE-1/SAFE-2.

weaknesses: F5's own wording pairs arrival 14:13:25 with cancellation 2 min 25 s later, which is below the default 3:01 threshold in NS-1 (iii); the 200 m radius itself is only the data-layer parameter (policy gap G2), not a published Ryde figure, so the rider can argue the driver was never properly 'at' the pickup point.

F6 undermines the '3 min up, cancelling the trip' message: counting from the driver's own tap (14:14:10) to cancellation (14:15:50) is only 1 min 40 s, so the rider can quote NS-2 and ask for a full $6.61 refund plus a flag_account for pressing 'I'm Here' and cancelling short of the waiting period.

NS-1 only credits pre-tap waiting if it was 'at the pickup point'; the rider can use F3 (stationary only 2 min 0 s, at 41 m) to argue the driver idled elsewhere and that the milestone chain (auto-arrival at 14:13:25, tap at 14:14:10) shows he rushed the arrival button.

The 38 m closest approach at 14:15:35 (F1) is at the very end of the stop, so it is no support for any earlier arrival claim, and the fare record F7 confirms $6.61 was actually charged, keeping the disputed sum live.

points.response: Not contested: F6 and F5 do distinguish a driver tap at 14:14:10 from a platform auto-arrival at 14:13:25, and I do not dispute the tap occurred. It does not help the driver, because NS-1 requires the wait to run after that tap, and the tap-to-cancel span is 1 min 40 s.
Not contested: F6 records 41 m from the pickup at the tap, so NS-1 (ii) is satisfied; my case has always been that element (iii) fails, not (ii).

The driver's arithmetic confirms my claim rather than refuting it: F5 pairs arrival at 14:13:25 with cancellation at 14:15:50 and states 2 min 25 s, which is itself below the > 3:01 required by NS-1 (iii). His own NS-4 citation is inapposite — NS-4 governs a rider cancelling an on-demand trip, and F4 records the cancellation was by the driver, so NS-0 routes this case to NS-1/NS-2.

The driver concedes the only contested element: every record of the post-tap wait — F6 (1 min 40 s) and F5 (2 min 25 s from the platform arrival) — falls short of NS-1 (iii), so under NS-2 the $6.61 charged per F7 must be refunded in full. F2 and F3 independently confirm he was inside 200 m only 2 min 25 s cumulatively and stationary only 2 min 0 s before cancelling, and F1's 38 m closest approach at 14:15:35 came at the very end of the stop.

I agree there is no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 trigger and I do not seek escalation on that basis; but a clean chat does not create the waiting time NS-1 (iii) demands, and F10's "3 min up" message is contradicted by the system clock in F6. The fee must still be refunded under NS-2, and F17 (one no-show dispute already upheld against this driver in 90 days) supports the ancillary flag_account request for his use of the arrival and cancellation buttons, which Ryde treats as fraud-flagged abuse.

To keep my own brief precise: I narrow C6 — the flag_account request rests on the NS-2 finding plus F17's prior upheld no-show dispute, and I do not rely on the rider's dispute count in F16 as the evidentiary basis, since the profile facts cannot decide the case on their own.

Conceded on the arithmetic: from the driver's own tap at 14:14:10 to the cancellation at 14:15:50 is 1 min 40 s, short of the >3 minutes NS-1 (iii) requires, so the fee cannot be sustained on that measure.

Conceded: on the rider's own measure the driver spent only 2 min 25 s within 200 m before cancelling (arrival 14:13:25, cancellation 14:15:50), and the stationary window was just 2 min 0 s at 41 m, so NS-1 (iii) is not met on any reading of the record.

Concede the point: the 14:15 message "3 min up, cancelling the trip" is contradicted by the timeline it sits inside (tap 14:14:10 → cancel 14:15:50 = 1 min 40 s), and statements yield to system records, so it cannot be relied on.

Conceded in substance: with NS-1 (i)(ii) satisfied but (iii) not, NS-2 refunds the $6.61 fee, and the amount is fixed by the cancellation-fee fact F7 with surge 1.0× (F8) confirming no other charge is in play.

This does not help either side on the cancellation fee — no traffic record (F13, F14) and fair weather (F15) simply means no extra condition bears on the NS-1/NS-2 timing issue, which is already decided against the driver.

An automatic-overcharge flag must not be treated as button abuse here: the driver's arrival was platform-confirmed (F5) before he tapped, he announced it openly in chat (F9), never pressed a waiting-fee claim, and his single prior upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F17) predates this one and cannot make this case 'repeated' — NS-2's flag is for pressing 'I'm Here' while outside the radius, which the 41 m record (F6) disproves.
